title: add VPC control plane terraform: multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, SGs, peering, Route53
author: Asha Patel
description: This PR adds Terraform plumbing to provision the Private Control Plane VPC for multi-AZ deployments. Motivation: enable fully automated VPC provisioning for Private deployments (VPC control plane) with secure interface endpoints, appropriate security groups, cross-account peering support, and Route53 private hosted zone delegations. The change set covers: 1) new terraform modules (vpc/control-plane, vpc/interface-endpoints, vpc/peering, vpc/route53-delegation) 2) examples for multi-az layouts and cross-account peering 3) upgrade hooks to reconcile existing clusters without downtime 4) docs and README updates with a recommended security posture and runbook. Checklist: - [x] Terraform modules implemented and unit-tested with local tflint/tfsec rules - [x] Integration example for AWS accounts + cross-account peering - [x] Helm chart values extension to accept provisioned VPC IDs and endpoints - [x] Upgrade hook that migrates existing control planes to new subnets with rolling replacement - [x] IAM least-privilege suggestions added to docs - [x] End-to-end smoke test run in staging (multi-az) Summary of risk and rollback: This is additive for new private control plane installs; for existing installs the upgrade hook is opt-in and performs a blue-green style replacement of control plane instances behind the same DNS. Rollback path included in terraform via stateful plan and documented manual steps. See linked linear tasks for rollout schedule and canary plan (ENG-8214).
commits: 6 commits: 1) init vpc/control-plane module (inputs: cidr, azs, shared_services_account) 2) add interface endpoints module and tested endpoints list 3) add peering module with cross-account route propagation and optional role assumption 4) route53 delegation workflows and kms-on-hosted-zone example 5) upgrade hook + post-upgrade smoke test 6) docs and examples: multi-az sample and troubleshooting notes
high_level_changes:
- Terraform modules added for control plane VPC provisioning (subnets, route tables, IGW/NAT where needed), interface endpoints (SSM, EC2, STS, KMS), security group templates for control plane and nodes, cross-account VPC peering module with route propagation toggles, Route53 private hosted zone delegation and optional KMS-backed encryption for zone records.
- Helm chart: added values to accept pre-provisioned VPC id, subnet ids, and endpoint ids to skip provisioning in case the operator manages infra separately.
- Installer: added an idempotent upgrade hook that can be used by operator to migrate control plane instances to newly created subnets with health checks and rollback on failure.
- Docs: architecture diagram, security recommendations, and step-by-step example for multi-account peering and Route53 delegation.

release_notes:
- Added terraform modules to provision Private Control Plane VPC with multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, peering, and Route53 delegation.
- Installer supports opt-in upgrade hook for migrating existing control planes to newly provisioned subnets.
- Helm chart accepts pre-provisioned VPC/subnet/endpoint IDs to support hybrid infra workflows.
notes: This PR is part of the multi-step rollout for private deployments (linked: ENG-8214). Operators must follow runbook for cross-account peering and add Route53 delegation records when performing production cutover.
manual_steps: 1) Run terraform plan in a sandbox account. 2) Validate endpoints and SGs with smoke tests. 3) Apply in control plane account. 4) For cross-account peering, follow runbook to accept peering request in the peer account and propagate routes. 5) Verify DNS resolution from peered account before cutover.
changelog_entry: Added: VPC control plane terraform modules (multi-az subnets, interface endpoints, peering, Route53 delegation); Installer upgrade hook for seamless migration; Helm values for pre-provisioned infra.
backout_plan: If post-upgrade issues are detected, run the included rollback script to re-register old control plane instances, revoke new subnets in the terraform state and destroy newly created resources created by the hook. Detailed steps in docs/runbooks/vpc-peering-runbook.md.
